newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks jump at opening on Wall St rally.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks jump at opening on Wall St rally.

text.p: The Australian share market opened firm on Monday but fell short of expected fresh highs in quiet trading after Friday's strong rally on Wall Street.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index was 16.4 points higher at 2,508.0.
Brokers said a bit more volume was needed to push the market above the record high of 2,515.1 points struck last Wednesday.
"It looks like it is going to go pretty close to it (record high)," said Gordon Furner, a broker at ABN AMRO Haore Govett.

Brokers said there was a lot of interest in John Fairfax as speculation rose that media baron Kerry Packer may make a long-rumoured bid for the newspaper group after he withdrew a deal to take management control of the Sydney Casino.

The threat of a nationwide one-day strike against BHP by unions, which was to be decided at a meeting later on Monday, was not having any negative impact on the steel and resource gaint's share price, brokers said.
News Corp shares were slightly firmer despite its U.S. satellite television venture being dealt a blow on Friday with the resignation of the venture's top executives.
Shares in Bougainville Copper surged on reports that secessionist rebels on the Papua New Guinea island of Bougainville would consider re-opening the dormant Panguna copper mine on the island.
